subject: english
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.**

The reporter said that an event had been organised for the President the previous day

options.text: The reporter said, “An event is organised for the President today.”
The reporter said, “An event is organised for the President yesterday.”
The reporter said, ”An event was organised for the President yesterday.”
The reporter said, “Let us organise an event for the President the next day.”

solution:
The correct answer is: **The reporter said, "An event was organised for the President yesterday."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Direct speech is when we report someone's words exactly as they were said.
 
• In reported speech, we introduced the statement with "**The reporter said that**." In direct speech, we remove this part.
 
• In direct speech, you need to enclose the reported statement in quotation marks to indicate that it is a direct quote.
 
• In reported speech, the past perfect tense "**had been organized**" was used because the event was in the past relative to the time of reporting.
 
• In direct speech, we change it to simple past tense to reflect the original statement's time frame: "**was organized**."
 
• In the reported speech version, the time reference "**the previous day**" was used to indicate when the event occurred.
 
• In direct speech, this time reference is retained: "**yesterday**."
 
• By following these steps, we have accurately transformed the sentence from reported speech back to its original form in direct speech, quoting what the reporter said.

Hence, the correct answer is **option 3**.
